title: First Jobs and Volunteer Work
text:
Last summer, thousands of young people in Spain took their first paid job in a restaurant, a shop or a hotel. Many of them found the work tiring, but it also taught them how to manage time and deal with customers. Some parents worry that a job might reduce study time. Others believe that earning a small salary encourages independence.

Volunteering offers a different kind of experience. In many cities, young people help at animal shelters, organize recycling days or teach reading to younger children. Such activities rarely pay, yet they often make a lasting impression on a future employer. As one volunteer explained, helping others made her feel useful for the first time.

questions.text: Where did many young people in Spain find their first paid job last summer?
According to paragraph two, what do young volunteers do?
options: They help at animal shelters, organize recycling days or teach reading.
They build roads and bridges in the city.
They sell products from door to door.

questions.text: What can be inferred about the parents who worry about part-time jobs?
options: They value studying and fear that work could reduce it.
They think teenagers should never leave school.
They want their children to earn as much money as possible.
They believe volunteering is more dangerous than working.

questions.text: Why does the author suggest that volunteering may help young people in the future?
options: It can make a good impression on employers who see it on a CV.
It guarantees a high salary after university.
It allows young people to avoid all paid work.
It replaces the need for school qualifications.

vocabulary.definition: to control or organize something successfully
the state of not depending on other people for money or decisions
the opinion or feeling that someone forms about a person or thing

paragraph_translations: El verano pasado, miles de jóvenes en España consiguieron su primer trabajo remunerado en un restaurante, una tienda o un hotel. Muchos de ellos encontraron el trabajo agotador, pero también aprendieron a gestionar el tiempo y a tratar con los clientes. Algunos padres temen que un empleo reduzca el tiempo de estudio. Otros creen que ganar un pequeño salario fomenta la independencia.

El voluntariado ofrece un tipo de experiencia diferente. En muchas ciudades, los jóvenes ayudan en protectoras de animales, organizan jornadas de reciclaje o enseñan a leer a niños pequeños. Estas actividades rara vez son remuneradas, pero a menudo causan una impresión duradera en un futuro empleador. Como explicó una voluntaria, ayudar a otros la hizo sentir útil por primera vez.
